input_files: practice_note_pn14_mechanics_liens.docx - the firm's practice note on mechanics lien claims on private works: who is a direct contractor, preliminary notice, completion and the notice of completion and the copies the owner has to give, the time to record, service of the claim, the amount of the lien, the four waiver and release forms, the 90 day enforcement period, the owner's remedies, and the counting conventions the office uses

claims_of_lien_larkspur_crossing.docx - the fifteen claims of mechanics lien recorded against the property, transcribed from the recorder's copies with each proof of service affidavit and the exhibits four claimants attached, three of them statements of account

owner_project_file_larkspur.xlsx - the owner's project file: the preliminary notices received, the waivers and releases received with each payment application, the owner's payments to the direct contractor with retention and the approved change orders, the agreements the owner signed itself, the subcontractor list with subcontract values, and the outgoing certified mail log

dk_subcontractor_payments.csv - the direct contractor's subcontractor payment ledger for the job, every check and stop payment entered against a subcontractor with its payment application, amount, and the date the check paid at the bank

completion_and_correspondence_larkspur.docx - the notice of completion as recorded, the construction manager's two memoranda on completion and on the copies of the notice, the email exchange among the owner, the direct contractor, and the firm, and the civil index and recorder searches
output_files: lien_analysis_larkspur_crossing.xlsx - the lien analysis workbook with the page for the partner and the two answers for the owner, the governing dates, the preliminary notice, notice of completion copy, and deadline tests, the waivers read against the payment ledger, each claim built up to its enforceable amount, the standing and bond for each claim, and the note to the partner
task_instruction:
Nadia at Piedmont Ridge wants the Larkspur Crossing liens dealt with before the refinance closes on November 20, and Marguerite has to tell her by the end of the month which claims we demand released and which the bank will make us bond. I'm the paralegal on the Piedmont Ridge account at Ferraro Whitcombe in Sacramento, California, and the first analysis on every lien file the office defends starts with me. I am in trial in Redding through the 16th, so I am handing this one to you because you have worked mechanics lien claims in this office for years and can read a waiver form against a check register without the Code open beside you. The file is in the folder: practice_note_pn14_mechanics_liens.docx, claims_of_lien_larkspur_crossing.docx, owner_project_file_larkspur.xlsx, dk_subcontractor_payments.csv, and completion_and_correspondence_larkspur.docx. The claims are our transcriptions of the recorder's copies with whatever each claimant attached, and the payments file is what Dunmore-Kettle's controller sent when Marguerite asked for it.

Build the analysis as one workbook named lien_analysis_larkspur_crossing.xlsx. The first tab is what Marguerite reads: for each recorded claim, whether the claimant has lien rights at all, whether the claim was recorded in time, what the waivers on file do to it, the amount the claimant could actually enforce against the property, what we do about it, and what a release bond would have to be for each lien we cannot clear. The same tab has to answer the two things Nadia asked in her email, whether the bonds fit inside the line her surety approved and whether the money Piedmont Ridge still holds on the Dunmore-Kettle contract covers what the claimants under that contract could enforce. Behind it I want the dates worked from the notice of completion under the practice note, the preliminary notices and the waivers checked claimant by claimant against the payments, and each enforceable amount built up so that Marguerite can follow every dollar to the claim or the ledger it came from. Put a note to Marguerite on the last tab with anything the file leaves open and anything that cuts against what Nadia expects. Nadia's position with the bank is that every claim is either late, waived, or Dunmore-Kettle's to answer, and if the record says otherwise Marguerite needs to hear it from us first. I need the workbook by Tuesday, October 20.

rubric.description: The workbook named lien_analysis_larkspur_crossing.xlsx states the standing of each of the 15 recorded claims on its first worksheet.

The first worksheet's release bonds required total reaches its value through a plain cell reference to the claim-by-claim standing behind it, or a sum over the same per-claim bonds alike, standing at $578,094.11.
Calder Drywall & Plaster's claim is found timely.
Calder Drywall & Plaster's last day to record is stated as 11/09/2026.
Capitol Wire & Lighting's claim is found timely.
Capitol Wire & Lighting's copy of the notice of completion is found given after the last day to give it.
The last day to record for a claimant given its copy of the notice of completion in time is stated as 09/28/2026.
Petrakis Plumbing's claim is found untimely.
The notice of completion is found effective under section 8182.
Sorensen Landscape is treated as a direct contractor.
Foothill Ready Mix's claim is kept with the claims to bond.
Lindqvist Fire Protection's claim is found served on the owner.
Sierra Pipe & Supply's enforceable amount is stated as $15,426.44 on the first worksheet.
Kastner Mechanical's enforceable amount is stated as $85,235 on the first worksheet.
Ostrowski Electric's enforceable amount is stated as $61,477 on the first worksheet.
Hedrick & Sons' enforceable amount is stated as $29,091.69 on the first worksheet.
Fenwick Roofing's claim is found released in full.
Abrego Glass & Glazing's claim is found not served on the owner.
Bautista Painting's enforceable amount is stated as $8,125 on the first worksheet.
The first worksheet states that the release bonds exceed the surety's line by $3,094.11.
The first worksheet states that the claims enforceable under the Dunmore-Kettle contract exceed the money the owner holds on it by $2,951.97.
The first worksheet answers that the release bonds do not fit inside the surety's line.
The first worksheet answers that the money the owner holds on the Dunmore-Kettle contract does not cover the claims enforceable under it.
The first worksheet routes 5 of the 15 recorded claims to a demand for release.
The money the owner holds on the Dunmore-Kettle contract is measured from the contract sum as adjusted by the approved change orders.
The note to Marguerite is the last worksheet.
The note tells Marguerite that the direct contractor can still record a claim until 11/09/2026.
The workbook wrongly treats the HVAC subcontractor's July draw as unpaid after check 4474 paid at the bank.
The workbook wrongly treats the painting subcontractor's unconditional waiver through 07/31/2026 as ineffective for want of payment.
The workbook wrongly treats the electrical subcontractor's final draw as paid by the unpaid check 4479.
The workbook wrongly denies the landscape contractor lien rights for want of a preliminary notice.
The workbook wrongly measures a release bond by the enforceable amount instead of the claim as recorded.
The workbook wrongly includes the lumber supplier's delivery of 05/08/2026 in its enforceable amount.
The workbook wrongly includes the lumber supplier's finance charges of $1,912.37 in its enforceable amount.
The workbook wrongly treats the drywall subcontractor's July release on the direct contractor's own form as releasing the July draw.
The workbook wrongly includes the plumbing supplier's delivery of 02/23/2026 in its enforceable amount.
The workbook wrongly includes the fire sprinkler subcontractor's change order request 3 of $9,467.50 in its enforceable amount.
Overall formatting and style of the deliverable as a lien analysis the partner can act on with the bank's counsel.
